purpose: Measured numbers for the two closed-loop questions the simulator used to leave as a disclosed gap: how much ethylene a crop stand produces, how sensitive lettuce is to it, and how much water a real life-support loop actually recovers. Every value is transcribed from a NASA source; none is estimated.

ethylene.whyItMatters: In a tightly closed chamber ethylene accumulates from the plants themselves. At 120 ppb it caused epinastic leaf rolling in wheat in NASA's Biomass Production Chamber, and independent chamber work shows lettuce dry weight falling at the same concentrations. A crop model that ignores it can overstate what a sealed habitat will produce.

production.source: Wheeler, Mackowiak, Stutte, Sager, Yorio, Ruffe, Fortier, Sharifi, Knott (1996), 'Ethylene production by plants in a closed environment', Advances in Space Research 18(4-5):163-166, doi:10.1016/0273-1177(95)00877-H, PMID 11538797. NASA Kennedy Space Center, CELSS Biomass Production Chamber (20 m2 stand, 113 m3).

peakProduction.appliesTo: rapid growth of lettuce and wheat stands

secondSource.citation: Wheeler et al. (2004), 'Ethylene production throughout growth and development of plants'
secondSource.peakProduction: 1.6-2.5 nmol m-2 d-1 during rapid growth of lettuce and wheat stands, about 0.3-0.5 nmol g-1 fresh weight per hour
secondSource.note: Tomato is the exception: a climacteric rise during ripening exceeded 500 ppb in the chamber.

lettuceDoseResponse.source: 'Effect of ethylene on growth of greenhouse lettuce at different light and temperature levels', Scientia Horticulturae, doi:10.1016/0304-4238(89)90082-4
lettuceDoseResponse.conditions: growth chambers, PPFD 50 / 100 / 150 umol m-2 s-1, 16-24 C

findings.note: effect generally largest in absolute terms at the two highest light levels

notes: The percentage effect was largest at the intermediate light level.
The effect was unaffected by temperature.
Reduced weight was related to reduced leaf size; ethylene generally increased leaf number.
lettuceDoseResponse.scopeNote: These are controlled-chamber dose-response measurements on lettuce, not a spaceflight measurement, and they are the only quantified lettuce ethylene dose-response recovered in this search.

relatedNasaReport.title: Monitoring ethylene emissions from plants cultured for a controlled ecological life support system
relatedNasaReport.finding: Ethylene accumulated to about 60 ppb in BPC wheat growouts; leaf flecking and rolling were virtually eliminated when potassium permanganate scrubbing was used.

notClaimed: No ethylene effect is applied inside the simulator's growth equations. The numbers above are served as a hazard screen next to the simulation, not folded into it.
No model of ethylene oxidation, leakage or scrubbing kinetics is offered: none was measured in a form that would support one.

water.source: NASA, 'NASA Achieves Water Recovery Milestone on International Space Station', 20 June 2023; ISS Environmental Control and Life Support System (ECLSS).

issRecovery.achievedBy: Brine Processor Assembly added to the Urine Processor Assembly in 2023
issRecovery.quote: Let's say you collect 100 pounds of water on the station. You lose two pounds of that and the other 98 percent just keeps going around and around.
issRecovery.attribution: Christopher Brown, ISS life support systems team

implication.note: NASA's figure for a four-person, 900-day Mars mission: about 12 tonnes of water without recycling, about 250 kg of make-up at 98 % closure.

water.useInSimulator: The simulator's water-recycling control is bounded by this measured range: 93-94 % is what the ISS recovered before the brine processor, 98 % is what it reaches now. Anything above 98 % is not a demonstrated capability.
